usage: This is the standard, everyday way to say "see you later" across the Levant. It is casual but perfectly acceptable in most professional settings among colleagues. The verb suffix must change depending on whether you are addressing a man, a woman, or a group.

variants.label: to a woman
variants.note: Use this when addressing a single female.

variants.label: to a group (Syrian/Lebanese)
variants.note: Use this when addressing two or more people in Syria or Lebanon.

variants.label: to a group (Jordanian/Palestinian)
variants.note: Use this when addressing two or more people in Jordan or Palestine.

variants.label: we will see you (to a man)
variants.note: Use this when you are speaking on behalf of yourself and others.

examples.english: I have to go now, see you later.
We'll talk tonight, see you later.
See you later at the cafe.
